hypotheses.text: RP101 does not exhibit an invariable, classic rod-cone photoreceptor ERG decline across all affected individuals; instead, full-field electroretinography displays distinct functional stages and patterns including electronegative ERGs indicating inner-retinal transmission defect, rod-cone dystrophy, or completely undetectable/extinguished responses in advanced disease.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the conflict over the binned claim of '100% rod-cone electroretinogram dysfunction'. Published cohorts explicitly identify electronegative ERGs (b-wave reduction out of proportion to a-wave) as well as unrecordable/extinguished ERGs rather than isolated photoreceptor rod-cone patterns.

evidence.text: In a series of 10 patients with CLN3-associated isolated retinal degeneration, electroretinography revealed a rod-cone pattern in 6 patients, but responses were completely undetectable in 2 patients.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: Electroretinography revealed a rod-cone pattern of dysfunction in 6 patients and were completely undetectable in 2 patients.

evidence.text: A 50-year-old female presenting with non-syndromic CLN3 retinal dystrophy demonstrated ERG responses that became electronegative over follow-up.

source.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of non-syndromic retinal dystrophy due to c.175G>A mutation in ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 3 (CLN3)
source.quote: ERG responses became electronegative and patient's serum contained anti-retinal antibodies.

evidence.text: In pediatric CLN3 presentations, electronegative ERGs were identified in all 5 patients assessed.

source.title: Early recognition of CLN3 disease facilitated by visual electrophysiology and multimodal imaging
source.quote: Electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients.

hypotheses.text: Isolated CLN3 retinal dystrophy (RP101) segregates into two distinct clinical subtypes based on age of onset and macular involvement rather than a single uniform phenotype: a severe early-onset form with early macular atrophy reaching legal blindness by the 40s, and a milder middle-age onset rod-cone degeneration with foveal preservation reaching legal blindness by the 70s.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the assertion of a 100% uniform presentation of early macular atrophy/bull's-eye maculopathy and constricted fields. Structural OCT and clinical progression bifurcate significantly based on genotype/age.

evidence.text: In a French cohort of 15 patients with isolated retinal degeneration due to biallelic CLN3 variants, two distinct disease patterns were delineated: 6 patients had mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset, while 9 patients had severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes.

source.title: Retinal Phenotype of Patients With Isolated Retinal Degeneration Due to CLN3 Pathogenic Variants in a French Retinitis Pigmentosa Cohort
source.quote: Two distinct patterns of retinal disease could be identified: a mild rod-cone degeneration of middle-age onset (n = 6; legal blindness threshold reached by 70s) and a severe retinal degeneration with early macular atrophic changes (n = 9; legal blindness threshold reached by 40s).

evidence.text: Ku et al. observed 4 patients with progressive late-onset rod-cone dystrophy (mean onset 29.7 years) who maintained focal foveal ellipsoid zone preservation on OCT, compared with 6 patients with earlier-onset disease (mean onset 12.1 years) showing widespread photoreceptor loss.

source.title: Detailed Clinical Phenotype and Molecular Genetic Findings in CLN3-Associated Isolated Retinal Degeneration
source.quote: Of the 10 patients, 4 had a progressive late-onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 29.7 (20-40) years, and 6 had an earlier onset rod-cone dystrophy, with a mean (range) age at onset of 12.1 (7-17) years.

hypotheses.text: An electronegative dark-adapted full-field ERG configuration is a highly sensitive discriminator distinguishing CLN3-associated early retinal degeneration from early-onset Stargardt disease (STGD1) and common nonsyndromic rod-cone dystrophies at presentation.
hypotheses.rationale: Early CLN3 retinal disease frequently masquerades as STGD1 or nonsyndromic macular/rod-cone dystrophy. Determining whether electronegative ERG is specific to CLN3 versus STGD1 provides an actionable clinical diagnostic discriminator.

evidence.text: In a comparative series, dark-adapted full-field ERGs were either absent or electronegative in CLN3 patients, whereas in early-onset STGD1 dark-adapted ERG responses were generally unaffected and none had an electronegative ERG.

source.title: Recognizing differentiating clinical signs of CLN3 disease (Batten disease) at presentation
source.quote: In CLN3 disease, dark-adapted (DA) full-field electroretinogram (ERG) responses were either absent or electronegative. In early-onset STGD1, DA ERG responses were generally unaffected. None of the STGD1 patients had an electronegative ERG.

new_directions.question_text: What specific CLN3 variant combinations dictate the bifurcation between mild late-onset rod-cone dystrophy with foveal preservation versus severe early-onset retinal degeneration with early macular atrophy?
new_directions.rationale: Smirnov et al. (2021) and Ku et al. (2017) demonstrated that nonsyndromic CLN3 phenotypes split into early and late onset groups with different genetic backgrounds. Clarifying allele-specific outcomes will refine diagnostic prognosis.

new_directions.question_text: What is the incidence and pathophysiological mechanism of the electronegative ERG pattern in nonsyndromic RP101, and does it reflect secondary bipolar cell/inner retinal synaptic pathology caused by CLN3 dysfunction?
new_directions.rationale: Electronegative ERG is uncommon in classic retinitis pigmentosa, pointing to synaptic or inner nuclear layer involvement. Determining its frequency across strictly nonsyndromic adult RP101 cohorts can validate its use as an early diagnostic differentiator.
